Index: attributed institutional diagnosis, foundations, sixty measures across constitutional order, Parliament, legislative quality, Senate/local government, executive, independent bodies, administration, constitutional court, prosecution, judicial career, judicial council and State council.
Index continuation: institutional chapters; no omitted annex identified.
Partisan institutional diagnosis begins. Criticism and causal/historical claims remain attributed publisher claims rather than independent fact.
Diagnosis continues: executive, Parliament and legal/institutional criticism. No new universal administrative entitlement or electoral mechanism inferred.
Diagnosis continues with independence/regeneration concerns and political rhetoric; no numerical bank value from general goals.
Concluding introduction commits PP to all measures and first-hundred-days legislative action. Implementation promise does not guarantee outcomes.

Explicit Cadiz, 23 January 2023 date. Principles 1-5: constitutional unity, criminal framework, most-voted list/local-government context, restore parliamentary functions. Local mayor election does not establish national Congress district.
Principles continue: Parliament, government accountability and Senate territorial functions; no replacement of Congress provincial representation.
Principles continue: rational executive structure, public expenditure, professional independent institutions and appointments. General independence alone does not define particular member selection.
Principles continue: constitutional court, prosecution and judicial independence. Retain distinction between institution mandates and every other court/office.
Principles conclude with judicial council and State council independence; detailed mechanisms follow. No blanket removal of all political appointment roles.

Measures 1-7: sedition, malversation and unlawful referendum offences; limited decree laws, ordinary legislative procedure and annual State of Nation debate. Publisher legal diagnosis remains attributed.

Measures 8-12: periodic government mandate reporting; sexual-law penalty reform; annual normative planning and public hearings; citizen economic costs; technical legislative quality office. No unsupported blanket provision-by-provision law position.

Measures 13-17: required consultative/technical reports for projects/proposals, homogeneous amendments, expert hearings, and public legislative influence sheet for each project/proposal identifying mediation/negotiation/amendments/voting. Full proposal-stage scope retained.
Measures 18-22: Senate territorial powers/fund control and most-voted municipal mayor rule/local governance reform. Distinct from national Congress single constituency.

Measures 23-27: secure public documents and economic reports, PM/opposition information, reasonable ministry/adviser structure, party-funded partisan travel. No open-format mandate from document security.
Measures 28-32: official aircraft register, proportional travel/electoral limits, accountable government transitions, professional public managers. No guaranteed absence of all discretion.
Measures 33-34: independent-body prior-political-role exclusion for five years; CNI qualifications/intelligence/cybersecurity. Institution and exact duration retained.

Measures 35-38: INE fixed presidency mandate, RTVE/EFE independence, professional CIS and quarterly political surveys of 2500, public-sector evaluation. Source claims about prior survey practice unverified.

Measure 39 across pages 21-22: efficient administration, common market, declarations/simplification, digitalisation/AI/data/robotics, transparency, open recruitment and incompatibilities. Generic digitisation does not define human final discretionary decisions or public document formats.

Completes measure39, remuneration next legislature; constitutional-court eligibility/candidacy thirty working days/professional suitability three-fifths begins. Distinguish public officials from doctors retirement.

Measures 40-42: court selection/transparency agenda/votes/code and preserved Congress/Senate/government/judicial-council appointment roles. Judicial origin election rule applies separately to judicial council.
Measures 43-45 constitutional procedure priorities/deadlines/remote exceptions/ethics and expanded prior constitutional review. No abolition of office-based special courts inferred.
Completes constitutional review; measures46-51 prosecutor independence begin, five-year term/twenty-year experience/five-year exclusion and recusation. Exact office scope retained.
Completes prosecutor measures: autonomous management, fiscal council six-member support, two-year delay before political return. Not all public-office incompatibilities.

Measures52-53: opposition-based entry,200 annual judges; judicial political leave/reentry thirty days, two years special nonjurisdictional services preserving rights/pay, reintegration. No judicial verdict inference.

Measures54-56: judicial senior appointments three-fifths, Supreme Court twenty years, removal of regional nomination terna; twelve judicial council members elected by active judges/magistrates,2 Supreme/3 over25years/7 others, prior political-role exclusion five years.

Measure56b: eight prestigious jurists appointed by Congress/Senate, distinct from twelve elected judicial-origin members; active-judiciary exclusion with four-year administrative exception. State council president25years/five-year political exclusion; required opinions with emergency exceptions; transparency begins.

Measures59-60 finish: State council publications/reports/accountability; more letrado posts and retirement age72. This is not the primary-care physician age rule. Final page fully read; no additional annex.
